:::{#thm-standard-basis-expansion}
#### A vector is a linear combination of indicator vectors

Every vector $\vx \in \reals^p$ is the linear combination
(@def-linear-combination) of the indicator vectors
$\vecf{e}_1, \ldots, \vecf{e}_p$ (@def-indicator-vector)
with coefficients $x_1, \ldots, x_p$:

$$\vx = \sum_{j=1}^{p} x_j \vecf{e}_j$$

:::

::: proof

Compare the two sides entry by entry. For each $i \in \{1, \ldots, p\}$:

$$
\ba
\paren{\sum_{j=1}^{p} x_j \vecf{e}_j}_i
&= \sum_{j=1}^{p} x_j (\vecf{e}_j)_i
&& \text{(@def-linear-combination, entry by entry)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{p}
   \begin{cases}
   x_j \cd 1 & \text{if } j = i \\
   x_j \cd 0 & \text{if } j \neq i
   \end{cases}
&& \text{(@def-indicator-vector)}
\\&= x_i
&& \text{(only the } j = i \text{ term is nonzero)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-standard-basis-expansion}
#### Expanding a vector in indicator vectors

$$
\sbmat{4 \\ -1 \\ 2}
= 4 \sbmat{1 \\ 0 \\ 0} + (-1) \sbmat{0 \\ 1 \\ 0} + 2 \sbmat{0 \\ 0 \\ 1}
= 4 \vecf{e}_1 - \vecf{e}_2 + 2 \vecf{e}_3
$$

:::
